text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistani police fought running battles with about 8,000 activists of the opposition Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) party trying to stage a protest outside parliament.
- Many Jamaat-i-Islami militants were injured in sporadic clashes with police in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore.
- The Lahore High Court asked the government to reply within four weeks against objections raised in a petition challenging the imposition of new taxes through an ordinance.
- Textile mill owners asked the government to let them import cotton from India and to instruct the state-run Cotton Export Corporation to import cotton from Central Asian states.
- Virus attack has caused severe damage to cotton crop in the central province of Punjab where at least two million 375-lb bales will be lost, sources said.
- Banque Indosuez and Societe Generale signed an agreement with the state-run Water and Power Development Authority to provide a commercial loan for the Chashma Hydro Power Project.
- The radical Islamic Taleban militia claimed that it controls the northwestern Afghanistan province of Badghis.
- Customs staff recovered 3.1 kg heroin from the baggage of a Ugandan lady flying to Muscat.
- Pakistan said it would not attend a regional conference Iran is hosting next week on the Afghan crisis, signalling sharp differences over the move between the two Islamic neighbours.
- The Jamaat-i-Islami party decided to continue its anti-government agitation and plans for a mass sit-in before parliament house on Monday.
